title: Bakery and Songbook
premise: Lena Iversen has spent ten years anonymously answering letters left in her bookshop's 'Dear Stranger' mailbox, never signing her name—until the letters' other half, widowed musician Theo Marsh, moves in next door and begins piecing together who she is. As their friendship deepens into love, Lena's fear of being truly known collides with the news that the bakery building housing both their businesses will be sold, forcing them to fight for the place that made their connection possible. When Theo finally discovers she was his anonymous correspondent all along, Lena must choose to claim him openly; they save the building together by turning it into a community co-op, and Lena learns that belonging means risking the whole heart.
about_author: G. M. Hartwell is a former small-town bookseller who writes warm romances about second chances and the families we build ourselves. Hartwell lives above a bakery, allegedly for research purposes only.

chapters.title: The Dear Stranger Box
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Opening on a rainy Tuesday, Lena closes the bookshop and finds a new letter in the old wooden box—a tradition started a decade ago when someone began leaving notes asking questions no one else would ask. She answers anonymously, as always. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Moving Vans and Minor Keys
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo Marsh, a widowed guitar teacher, moves into the apartment next to the bookshop with his daughter June and a truckload of sheet music. He notices the woman in the window who doesn't wave back. Emotional beat: cautious hope after grief.

chapters.title: Flour on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The bakery downstairs leaves day-old cinnamon rolls at Lena's door, and Mrs. Okonkwo the baker nudges her toward the new neighbor. Lena deflects, but June wanders into the shop and devours three picture books. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth cracking the surface.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Questions
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Sorting boxes, Theo rereads the letters he received from 'the stranger' over the years—the ones that got him through his wife's illness. He wonders if the box still exists. Emotional beat: longing for an unknown friend.

chapters.title: A Borrowed Umbrella
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A storm strands Theo at the bookshop closing time; Lena lends him an umbrella and, flustered, lies that she's busy most evenings. Her son Eli and June bond instantly over comic books. Emotional beat: attraction met with self-protection.

chapters.title: The Landlord's Letter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Both receive notice: the building housing the bakery, bookshop, and apartments is for sale to a developer. Theo proposes the tenants meet; Lena resists organizing anything. Emotional beat: dread of losing the ground beneath everything.

chapters.title: Open Mic, Closed Heart
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the bakery's open mic, Theo performs a song he admits he wrote for someone he's never met. Lena recognizes the lyrics echo her own anonymous replies and nearly flees. Emotional beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: What Eli Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Eli, twelve, asks why they never visit anyone or let anyone visit them. Lena realizes her invisibility has become his inheritance. She agrees to the tenant meeting. Emotional beat: maternal reckoning.

chapters.title: Committee of Misfits
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The first save-the-building meeting: Mrs. Okonkwo, Lena, Theo, the cobbler, and a retired teacher draft a co-op plan. Theo and Lena stay late, talking until midnight. Emotional beat: found family assembling itself.

chapters.title: Letters, Unsigned
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo writes a new letter to the stranger describing the woman next door who makes him feel awake again—and asks whether it's betrayal to want more than paper. Lena reads it that night, shaking. Emotional beat: the two halves of his heart colliding.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A near-kiss in the bookshop stacks interrupted by a customer. Lena pulls back, insisting she's bad timing personified. Theo, hurt, retreats. Emotional beat: the cost of half-measures.

chapters.title: June's Question
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. June asks if Lena can be her mom's replacement—not exactly, but close enough to terrify Theo, who fears loving again means losing again. He decides to stop writing to the stranger. Emotional beat: grief masquerading as caution.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The developer offers Lena individually a generous buyout to vacate early—an offer sized to tempt a struggling single mother. She hides it from the group. Emotional beat: temptation and shame.

chapters.title: Bank Meeting, Broken Nerve
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The co-op's loan application stalls; the bank wants proof of committed buyers. Theo publicly praises Lena's leadership; she feels like a fraud holding her secret buyout letter. Emotional beat: guilt tightening.

chapters.title: Confession in the Cold
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Mrs. Okonkwo discovers the hidden offer and confronts Lena gently: you keep choosing to be unchosen rather than risk choosing yourself. Lena walks home through snow past the lit windows of people who count on her. Emotional beat: the mask slipping.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cleaning out the shop's back room, Theo finds Lena's handwriting on an old reply draft—identical to the stranger's. He says nothing, stunned, and goes home to write one final letter addressed not to a stranger but to her name. Emotional beat: revelation held like a live coal.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At the emergency tenant meeting, Theo reads the final letter aloud, then looks straight at Lena and speaks her name. Publicly exposed, she confesses everything—including the buyout offer—and asks forgiveness. Emotional beat: climax; total exposure, total vulnerability.

chapters.title: Silence Between Verses
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo doesn't speak to Lena for three days. June and Eli conspire miserably. Finally Theo appears at her door: he isn't angry that she hid—he's angry she believed she had to earn belonging. Emotional beat: rupture becoming repair.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena tears up the developer's offer and signs the co-op papers alongside the others; the bank approves, moved by the community's pledges. The building is saved. Emotional beat: triumph earned collectively.

chapters.title: Whole Heart, Sung Out Loud
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the spring open mic, Theo premieres a song titled 'Lena,' and she takes the stage beside him—the first time she's been visible on purpose. They kiss to applause and flour dust. Emotional beat: joy without apology.

chapters.title: Two Doors Open
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Months later: the wall between the bookshop and Theo's music room comes down; Eli and June argue happily over whose house rules apply. Lena writes a signed letter to the Dear Stranger box thanking whoever started it. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Dear Stranger, Signed
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. One year on, a new lonely newcomer leaves a letter in the box; Lena and Theo answer it together, signed this time, and invite her to Sunday dinner. The last line mirrors the novel's first. Emotional beat: the circle opened outward—belonging offered forward.
